Have you ever caught yourself wondering about what really happens after we die? Maybe it’s a passing thought, a quiet curiosity, or even a question that pops up in the middle of an awkward conversation. You’re definitely not alone.
In Will My Cat Eat My Eyeballs? And Other Questions About Dead Bodies, Caitlin Doughty invites us to lean into those strange, fascinating, and sometimes downright quirky questions we all secretly have about death. Together, we’ll pull back the curtain on the mysteries surrounding what happens to our bodies, the traditions that shape our goodbyes, and the odd—but honest—curiosities that both kids and adults aren’t afraid to ask.
What if we could talk openly about death, stripping away fear and making room for a little wonder—or even laughter? Through Caitlin’s eyes, the world of mortuary science isn’t just about biology and rituals. It’s about connecting the dots between science, culture, and our very human emotions.
On this journey, we’ll discover how the practical side of decomposition, the strangeness of funeral customs, and the myths we cling to all reveal something bigger: that understanding death can actually bring us closer together—and even help us embrace life with a little more curiosity and courage.
So, as we get ready to explore the unexpected, let’s keep an open mind. Who knows? We might just find comfort, connection, and maybe even a few surprises in the one topic most of us try to avoid. Welcome to this journey—let’s see what we can discover together.
